faqs.question: How frequently do classes meet, and must I attend all day?
faqs.answer:
Classes meet in person two Saturdays per month. Students select either:

Morning session: 9 a.m. – 12 p.m.
Afternoon session: 1 p.m. – 4 p.m.
In-person attendance is required for program eligibility.

If a student is completing two micro credentials at once, they can attend both morning and afternoon sessions for that day.

faqs.question: Are classes primarily online or face-to-face?
faqs.answer:
The 10 K program is a hybrid format:
Most coursework is completed online
But students must attend in-person sessions twice per month in DFW or El Paso for the micro credentials

 If you require a fully online program with no in-person requirements, consider Texas Tech’s Online Plus programs.

faqs.question: When can I start the program?
faqs.answer: Courses start every two weeks, allowing students to begin at multiple points throughout the year. An advisor can assist in selecting a custom start date.

faqs.question: How long does it take to complete the 10 K program?
faqs.answer:
The program can be completed in as little as one year, depending on your prior coursework and study pace.
Each micro-credential course lasts approximately 4 weeks.

faqs.question: What happens if I have fewer than 80 credit hours?
faqs.answer:
Students with 70–79 credit hours can still enroll, but the total cost may exceed $10,000 (usually still under $15,000).
Students with 60–69 credit hours may qualify for a different Texas Tech degree program, or work with an advisor to develop a plan utilizing community college courses or self-paced courses to get to 70 transferable hours.
Students with fewer than 60 credit hours should speak with an advisor to discuss alternative options.
This program is specifically for students who already have significant prior college credits.

faqs.question: What is the maximum number of credits I can transfer?
faqs.answer:
You may transfer up to 90 college credit hours into the 10k program, provided that a minimum of 10-degree applicable hours are upper division and from a four-year institution. If you have more than 90 credits but haven’t earned a degree, you can still apply.
Credits are preliminarily evaluated individually for transfer eligibility. Transfer eligibility is subject to change upon admittance to TTU.
Please note Texas Tech does not accept Workforce education or vocational courses as transferable hours. However, students can inquire about a B.A.A.S. degree if the hours are applicable.

faqs.question: Will the 21 hours I earn throughout the 10 K program count towards the 70 transferable hours?
faqs.answer: No, an advisor will work with you to get a plan in place for getting up to 70 hours.

faqs.question: What are the admission requirements for the 10 K program?
faqs.answer:
Applicants must meet the following criteria:
Have completed at least 70 transferable college credit hours.
Be able to attend in-person classes twice per month at a Texas location (DFW or El Paso) for micro credentials only.

Please note that you do not have to be core complete. If you are not core complete, this will only affect your pricing.

This program is not designed for students who cannot attend in person micro credential classes two Saturdays a month, in order to earn 12 hours of course credit.

faqs.question: Do I have to live in Dallas/Fort Worth or El Paso to join the program?
faqs.answer:
No, but you must attend in-person classes two Saturdays per month at one of these locations:

 Dallas/Fort Worth (DFW) – 4201 State Highway 161, Suite 250, Irving, TX 75038
 El Paso – 5001 El Paso Drive, El Paso, TX 79905

 All other coursework is completed online, but in-person sessions are mandatory.

faqs.question: Are students actively taking courses at Texas Tech eligible for the 10 K program?
faqs.answer: No, current active Texas Tech students are not eligible for the 10 K program.

faqs.question: Is the 10 K program available for international students?
faqs.answer: No, this program is not currently available for international students.

faqs.question: What career benefits can I expect after completing the 10 K program?
faqs.answer:
Graduates of the 10 K Degree Completion Program typically experience:
Improved career prospects
Better opportunities for advancement
Increased earning potential

This program is designed to help students finish a degree they started previously, allowing them to qualify for better jobs and career growth opportunities.

faqs.question: Can I walk the stage in Lubbock for graduation?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can walk the stage in Texas Tech’s commencement ceremony upon completion of the program.

faqs.question: How do I start the enrollment process?
faqs.answer: I can collect your basic information now and schedule a meeting with an advisor, who will guide you through the enrollment process.

faqs.question: What is the 10 K Degree Completion Program?
faqs.answer:
The 10 K Degree Completion Program is an affordable, hybrid program designed for students with at least 70 college credit hours who want to complete a Bachelor of Science in Leadership Studies or a Bachelor of Arts in University Studies.

This program requires in-person class attendance twice per month in Texas (DFW or El Paso) to complete the micro credentials.

faqs.question: What degrees can I earn through the 10 K program?
faqs.answer:
Students can complete one of the following degrees:
Bachelor of Science in Leadership Studies
Bachelor of Arts in University Studies

faqs.question: What are the main advantages of the 10 K program?
faqs.answer:
Affordable – Designed to be completed for $10,000 or less.
 Accelerated – Short 4-week courses allow for fast degree completion.
 Hybrid Learning – Online coursework + in-person support.
 Personalized Support – Advisors and faculty provide individualized guidance.
 Designed for Working Adults – Flexible schedule with part-time and full-time options.
Unlike Online Plus, the 10 K program is specifically structured for students completing degrees with prior credits and in-person learning.

faqs.question: How much does the 10 K program cost? Are there additional fees?
faqs.answer:
The total cost is $10,000 or less for qualified students. There is a $2,000.00 conversion fee for the 21 hours earned through micro credentials and prior learning experience credits. Students are then billed per credit hour at Texas Tech for remaining course work.

 You can get started in the first four micro-credential courses for free and pay later when you convert them to credit. Also, all eligible prior-learning credits will convert to credit for no cost.

Your advisor will provide an exact cost estimate based on your transfer credits and course load.

faqs.question: When is the $2,000 conversion fee due?
faqs.answer: When you have been admitted to Texas Tech, Student Business Services will include this fee into your semester bill.

faqs.question: Can Financial Aid cover the $2,000 conversion fee?
faqs.answer: The $2,000 fee is an out of pocket expense.
